blocks.en: 1. The Question Before the Question
blocks.es_reference: 1. La pregunta antes de la pregunta

blocks.en: Before a pastor asks what a passage means, he must ask one earlier question: what kind of writing am I reading? The Bible is not one genre. It is a library of many genres bound between two covers — letters, royal chronicles, poetry, visionary apocalypse, wisdom sayings, gospel narratives, theological history. Each has its own reading rules. Treat a poem as a propositional argument and you will misread it. Treat a parable as a chronicle and you will misread it. Treat a prophet’s symbolic action as a private domestic anecdote and you will lose the whole sermon he was preaching with his life.
blocks.es_reference: Antes de que un pastor pregunte qué significa un pasaje, debe hacer una pregunta anterior: ¿qué clase de escritura estoy leyendo? La Biblia no es un solo género. Es una biblioteca de muchos géneros encuadernados entre dos tapas — cartas, crónicas reales, poesía, apocalipsis visionario, dichos sapienciales, narrativas evangélicas, historia teológica. Cada uno tiene sus propias reglas de lectura. Trate un poema como un argumento proposicional y lo malinterpretará. Trate una parábola como una crónica y la malinterpretará. Trate la acción simbólica de un profeta como una anécdota doméstica privada y perderá todo el sermón que él predicaba con su vida.

blocks.en: This is the principle of this unit. Genre determines interpretation. Identify the kind of literature before you ask what it means, and the passage will open to you in its own way. Force every passage into the same reading template and you will distort more than you preach.
blocks.es_reference: Éste es el principio de esta unidad. El género determina la interpretación. Identifique la clase de literatura antes de preguntar qué significa, y el pasaje se le abrirá a su manera. Fuerce cada pasaje al mismo molde de lectura y distorsionará más de lo que predica.

blocks.en: 2. The Six Main Biblical Genres
blocks.es_reference: 2. Los seis principales géneros bíblicos

blocks.en: Six broad categories cover most of the Bible. Narrative: Genesis, Joshua, Judges, Ruth, Samuel, Kings, the Gospels, Acts. These tell stories; they show theology in action rather than stating it as doctrine. Law: the legal sections of Exodus through Deuteronomy. These give commandments and statutes for a covenant people in a particular moment of redemptive history. Wisdom: Job, Proverbs, Ecclesiastes, Song of Solomon. These reflect on how the world works under God’s rule. Poetry: the Psalms, Lamentations, and large portions of the prophets. These speak in compressed images, parallel lines, and emotion. Prophecy: Isaiah through Malachi, plus Revelation. These confront God’s people with covenant warnings and covenant promises, often with symbolic actions or visions. Epistles: Romans through Jude. These are pastoral letters written to particular churches with particular problems.
blocks.es_reference: Seis categorías amplias cubren la mayor parte de la Biblia. Narrativa: Génesis, Josué, Jueces, Rut, Samuel, los Reyes, los Evangelios, Hechos. Cuentan historias; muestran la teología en acción en lugar de declararla como doctrina. Ley: las secciones legales de Éxodo a Deuteronomio. Dan mandamientos y estatutos para un pueblo del pacto en un momento particular de la historia redentiva. Sabiduría: Job, Proverbios, Eclesiastés, Cantares. Reflexionan sobre cómo funciona el mundo bajo el gobierno de Dios. Poesía: los Salmos, Lamentaciones, y grandes porciones de los profetas. Hablan en imágenes comprimidas, líneas paralelas, y emoción. Profecía: Isaías a Malaquías, además de Apocalipsis. Confrontan al pueblo de Dios con advertencias y promesas del pacto, a menudo con acciones simbólicas o visiones. Epístolas: Romanos a Judas. Son cartas pastorales escritas a iglesias particulares con problemas particulares.

blocks.en: Each has its own reading rules. The pastor who treats a Proverb as if it were an absolute promise will be wounded when his obedient parenting still produces a wayward son. The pastor who treats an apocalyptic vision as a newspaper headline will produce timelines that frighten his people and embarrass the Lord. Genre is the corrective.
blocks.es_reference: Cada uno tiene sus propias reglas de lectura. El pastor que trata un Proverbio como si fuera una promesa absoluta será herido cuando su crianza obediente todavía produzca un hijo descarriado. El pastor que trata una visión apocalíptica como un titular de periódico producirá cronogramas que asusten a su pueblo y avergüencen al Señor. El género es el correctivo.

blocks.en: A word about this map before you use it: six categories are a teaching simplification, not a strict filing system, and two things deserve their own mention. First, apocalyptic is not simply prophecy with more excitement. Revelation, Daniel's visions, and portions of Ezekiel and Zechariah share a distinct set of conventions — symbolic numbers, cosmic imagery, visions mediated by an angelic guide — that call for their own reading rules, different from a prophet like Amos standing in the marketplace and pronouncing covenant warnings in plain speech. Second, the Gospels are narrative, but they are not narrative in the same sense as Judges or Ruth; each Gospel writer is shaping real history into proclamation, selecting and arranging material to answer the question who is this Man? Finally, remember that a single book often contains more than one genre within it — Isaiah moves between oracle, narrative, and apocalyptic vision; Daniel is half court narrative and half apocalyptic dream. Ask the genre question at the level of the passage in front of you, not only at the level of the book's title page.
blocks.es_reference: Una palabra sobre este mapa antes de usarlo: seis categorías son una simplificación pedagógica, no un sistema estricto de archivo, y dos cosas merecen su propia mención. Primero, lo apocalíptico no es simplemente profecía con más emoción. Apocalipsis, las visiones de Daniel, y porciones de Ezequiel y Zacarías comparten un conjunto distinto de convenciones — números simbólicos, imágenes cósmicas, visiones mediadas por un guía angelical — que piden sus propias reglas de lectura, distintas de un profeta como Amós de pie en la plaza pronunciando advertencias del pacto en habla llana. Segundo, los Evangelios son narrativa, pero no son narrativa en el mismo sentido que Jueces o Rut; cada evangelista está dando forma a historia real convertida en proclamación, seleccionando y organizando el material para responder la pregunta ¿quién es este Hombre? Finalmente, recuerde que un solo libro a menudo contiene más de un género dentro de sí — Isaías se mueve entre oráculo, narrativa, y visión apocalíptica; Daniel es mitad narrativa de corte y mitad sueño apocalíptico. Haga la pregunta del género al nivel del pasaje que tiene delante, no solo al nivel de la portada del libro.

blocks.en: 3. Hosea — Prophecy as Enacted Biography
blocks.es_reference: 3. Oseas: la profecía como biografía representada

blocks.en: Some things seem unforgivable. The book of Hosea opens with one of them. God commands an eighth-century prophet to do something no modern reader can flatten into a domestic anecdote:
blocks.es_reference: Algunas cosas parecen imperdonables. El libro de Oseas abre con una de ellas. Dios manda a un profeta del siglo octavo a hacer algo que ningún lector moderno puede aplanar a una anécdota doméstica:

blocks.en: “Go, take yourself a wife of harlotry and children of harlotry, for the land has committed great harlotry by departing from the LORD.” (Hosea 1:2, NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: «Vé, tómate una mujer fornicaria, é hijos de fornicaciones; porque la tierra se dará á fornicar apartándose de Jehová.» (Oseas 1:2, RVG)

blocks.en: Hosea obeys. He marries Gomer, a prostitute. They have three children. The first is named Jezreel, meaning God will scatter. The second is Lo-Ruhamah, meaning not pitied. The third is Lo-Ammi, meaning not My people. Gomer leaves Hosea and returns to her old life. She eventually sells herself into slavery. And then comes the second command in chapter three: Go again and love this woman. Hosea walks to the slave market. Slaves were sold naked on the auction block. Hosea’s own wife stands naked before a courtyard of rowdy men. Hosea enters the bidding. He buys her back for fifteen pieces of silver and a homer and a half of barley — half the normal price for a slave. Sin had taken its toll on what she fetched at auction. He pays the price, takes her home, and loves her again.
blocks.es_reference: Oseas obedece. Se casa con Gomer, una prostituta. Tienen tres hijos. El primero se llama Jezreel, que significa Dios esparcirá. La segunda es Lo-Ruhama, que significa no compadecida. El tercero es Lo-Ammi, que significa no pueblo Mío. Gomer deja a Oseas y regresa a su vida anterior. Eventualmente se vende a la esclavitud. Y luego viene el segundo mandato en el capítulo tres: Vé otra vez, y ama a esa mujer. Oseas camina al mercado de esclavos. Los esclavos se vendían desnudos en el bloque de subasta. La propia esposa de Oseas se para desnuda ante un patio lleno de hombres bulliciosos. Oseas entra en la puja. La compra de vuelta por quince piezas de plata y un homer y medio de cebada — la mitad del precio normal para una esclava. El pecado había hecho mella en lo que ella valía en la subasta. Paga el precio, se la lleva a casa, y la ama de nuevo.

blocks.en: Ask the genre question. If Hosea is autobiography, this is a heartbreaking story about one ancient pastor’s difficult marriage. The reader may pity Hosea, admire his patience, and move on. But Hosea is not autobiography. Hosea is prophecy, and biblical prophecy regularly uses symbolic actions to deliver covenant messages. Isaiah walked barefoot for three years as a sign against Egypt. Jeremiah wore a wooden yoke around his neck. Ezekiel lay on his side for over a year. Hosea’s entire marriage is a prophetic sign. The marriage is the sermon.
blocks.es_reference: Haga la pregunta del género. Si Oseas es autobiografía, ésta es una historia desgarradora sobre el difícil matrimonio de un pastor antiguo. El lector puede compadecer a Oseas, admirar su paciencia, y seguir adelante. Pero Oseas no es autobiografía. Oseas es profecía, y la profecía bíblica usa regularmente acciones simbólicas para entregar mensajes del pacto. Isaías caminó descalzo durante tres años como señal contra Egipto. Jeremías llevó un yugo de madera alrededor del cuello. Ezequiel se acostó de un lado durante más de un año. El matrimonio entero de Oseas es una señal profética. El matrimonio es el sermón.

blocks.en: 4. What Hosea’s Genre Unlocks
blocks.es_reference: 4. Lo que el género de Oseas desbloquea

blocks.en: Once you recognize the genre, every painful detail becomes theology. Gomer is Israel. Hosea is God. Israel has played the harlot, chasing after Baal and other gods. The children’s names announce judgment: God will scatter, no longer pitied, not My people. Israel’s descent into spiritual slavery is Gomer’s descent into literal slavery. The price Hosea pays at the auction is the price God pays to redeem an unfaithful people. The hardest line in the book is God’s second command: Go again, and love this woman. No human heart would do that. No human husband should be required to. But the genre tells us why God required it. He was preaching His own covenant love through Hosea’s broken life. God Himself was modeling what He was about to do for Israel.
blocks.es_reference: Una vez que reconoce el género, cada detalle doloroso se vuelve teología. Gomer es Israel. Oseas es Dios. Israel ha jugado a la prostituta, persiguiendo a Baal y otros dioses. Los nombres de los hijos anuncian juicio: Dios esparcirá, ya no compadecida, no Mi pueblo. El descenso de Israel a la esclavitud espiritual es el descenso de Gomer a la esclavitud literal. El precio que Oseas paga en la subasta es el precio que Dios paga para redimir a un pueblo infiel. La línea más dura del libro es el segundo mandato de Dios: Vé otra vez, y ama a esa mujer. Ningún corazón humano haría eso. Ningún esposo humano debería ser requerido a hacerlo. Pero el género nos dice por qué Dios lo requirió. Estaba predicando Su propio amor del pacto a través de la vida quebrantada de Oseas. Dios mismo estaba modelando lo que estaba a punto de hacer por Israel.

blocks.en: Read Hosea without the prophetic genre and you will end up debating whether God ethically commanded a man to marry a known prostitute. Read it with the genre and you stop debating and start trembling. God is the One who buys back what shame has unmade. That is the gospel of Hosea, and it is preached in a marriage rather than in a sermon.
blocks.es_reference: Lea Oseas sin el género profético y terminará debatiendo si Dios mandó éticamente a un hombre casarse con una prostituta conocida. Léalo con el género y deja de debatir y comienza a temblar. Dios es Aquel que recompra lo que la vergüenza ha deshecho. Ése es el evangelio de Oseas, y se predica en un matrimonio en lugar de en un sermón.

blocks.en: 5. Ruth — Narrative as Theological Story
blocks.es_reference: 5. Rut: la narrativa como historia teológica

blocks.en: Open the book of Ruth and you are in a different genre entirely. No symbolic action. No vision. No covenant lawsuit. Just a story. A famine drives a Bethlehem family to Moab. The father dies. The two sons marry Moabite women and die. Three widows are left. One returns to her people. The other — Ruth — clings to her mother-in-law and follows her back to Bethlehem, where she gleans in the field of a wealthy kinsman named Boaz. He notices her. He marries her. They have a son named Obed, who becomes the grandfather of King David. Four chapters. One love story. A whole theology of redemption.
blocks.es_reference: Abra el libro de Rut y está en un género completamente distinto. Ninguna acción simbólica. Ninguna visión. Ningún juicio del pacto. Solamente una historia. Una hambruna lleva a una familia de Belén a Moab. El padre muere. Los dos hijos se casan con mujeres moabitas y mueren. Tres viudas quedan. Una regresa a su pueblo. La otra — Rut — se aferra a su suegra y la sigue de vuelta a Belén, donde espiga en el campo de un pariente acaudalado llamado Boaz. Él la nota. Se casa con ella. Tienen un hijo llamado Obed, que llega a ser el abuelo del rey David. Cuatro capítulos. Una historia de amor. Toda una teología de la redención.

blocks.en: Narrative is a real genre with real rules. One rule is that the narrator usually does not announce the theology aloud — he embeds it in the names, the details, the structure. Look at the names. Elimelech means my God is King. Naomi means pleasure. Mahlon means sick. Chilion means pining away. Pleasure’s sons are sick and pining away; that is no accident. Ruth means beauty. When Naomi returns to Bethlehem she asks to be renamed Mara, meaning bitter: do not call me Pleasure; call me Bitter, because the Almighty has dealt bitterly with me. The narrator is preaching, but he preaches through the names, not above them.
blocks.es_reference: La narrativa es un género real con reglas reales. Una regla es que el narrador generalmente no anuncia la teología en voz alta — la encarna en los nombres, los detalles, la estructura. Mire los nombres. Elimelec significa mi Dios es Rey. Noemí significa placer. Mahlón significa enfermo. Quelión significa desfalleciendo. Los hijos de Placer son enfermo y desfalleciendo; eso no es accidente. Rut significa belleza. Cuando Noemí regresa a Belén pide ser renombrada Mara, que significa amarga: no me llaméis Noemí, sino llamadme Mara: porque en grande amargura me ha puesto el Todopoderoso. El narrador está predicando, pero predica a través de los nombres, no por encima de ellos.

blocks.en: A second rule is that structure carries weight. Ruth begins with three deaths in Moab and ends with a birth in Bethlehem. The famine of chapter one is gone by chapter four. The bitterness of the opening becomes the blessing of the close. Naomi has a son, the women of Bethlehem say at the end — about a grandson in the line of the Messiah. Genre teaches you to read the story as the story it is, and to let the redemption it embodies emerge from the shape of the four chapters rather than from one proof-verse in the middle.
blocks.es_reference: Una segunda regla es que la estructura carga peso. Rut comienza con tres muertes en Moab y termina con un nacimiento en Belén. La hambruna del capítulo uno se ha ido en el capítulo cuatro. La amargura de la apertura se vuelve la bendición del cierre. Noemí tiene un hijo, dicen las mujeres de Belén al final — sobre un nieto en la línea del Mesías. El género le enseña a leer la historia como la historia que es, y a dejar que la redención que encarna emerja de la forma de los cuatro capítulos en lugar de un solo versículo de prueba en el medio.

blocks.en: 6. The Same Truth in Two Genres
blocks.es_reference: 6. La misma verdad en dos géneros

blocks.en: Now hold Hosea and Ruth side by side. Then add a third book — Luke 15, the Prodigal Son. Notice what the Spirit has done. The same gospel of unforgivable forgiveness is preached in three different genres. In Hosea, it is preached as prophetic enacted biography — the prophet’s real marriage is the visible sermon. In Ruth, it is preached as theological narrative — one family’s loss and restoration ends in the line of David. In Luke 15, it is preached as parable — a story Jesus tells to grumbling Pharisees. Same gospel. Three genres. Each genre lands the truth a different way.
blocks.es_reference: Ahora sostenga a Oseas y a Rut lado a lado. Luego añada un tercer libro — Lucas 15, el Hijo Pródigo. Note lo que el Espíritu ha hecho. El mismo evangelio del perdón imperdonable se predica en tres géneros distintos. En Oseas, se predica como biografía profética representada — el matrimonio real del profeta es el sermón visible. En Rut, se predica como narrativa teológica — la pérdida y restauración de una familia termina en la línea de David. En Lucas 15, se predica como parábola — una historia que Jesús cuenta a fariseos murmuradores. El mismo evangelio. Tres géneros. Cada género hace aterrizar la verdad de manera distinta.

blocks.en: The Prodigal Son and Gomer are sometimes set against each other. There is one important difference. The Prodigal son came to himself and repented. Gomer never says she is sorry — the text simply tells us that her husband bought her back and loved her again. In one genre, redemption is preached through the sinner’s return. In another, redemption is preached through the husband’s pursuit. Both are true. Both are necessary. Each genre tells the truth that its form was built to tell. Try to flatten the genres into one and you lose the texture by which the Bible preaches God’s love from every angle.
blocks.es_reference: El Hijo Pródigo y Gomer a veces se colocan uno contra el otro. Hay una diferencia importante. El hijo pródigo volvió en sí y se arrepintió. Gomer nunca dice que lo siente — el texto simplemente nos dice que su esposo la compró de vuelta y la amó de nuevo. En un género, la redención se predica a través del retorno del pecador. En otro, la redención se predica a través de la búsqueda del esposo. Ambas son ciertas. Ambas son necesarias. Cada género dice la verdad que su forma fue edificada para decir. Trate de aplanar los géneros en uno y perderá la textura por la cual la Biblia predica el amor de Dios desde cada ángulo.

blocks.en: 7. Poetry, Wisdom, and the Trap of Flattening
blocks.es_reference: 7. La poesía, la sabiduría, y la trampa del aplanamiento

blocks.en: Hebrew poetry has its own grammar. Lines come in parallel pairs — the second line restates, intensifies, or contrasts the first. Imagery is compressed. Emotion is given room to speak. Why have You forsaken me? in Psalm 22 is a poet’s cry, not a doctrinal statement about divine abandonment. The LORD is my shepherd, I shall not want in Psalm 23 is a metaphor; David is not literally a sheep. Read the Psalms as flat doctrinal propositions and you will preach abstractions where the Psalmist meant to wring tears. Read them as poetry — with image and feeling and form intact — and they will teach your people to pray.
blocks.es_reference: La poesía hebrea tiene su propia gramática. Las líneas vienen en pares paralelos — la segunda línea reformula, intensifica, o contrasta la primera. Las imágenes son comprimidas. La emoción tiene espacio para hablar. ¿Por qué me has desamparado? en el Salmo 22 es el grito de un poeta, no una declaración doctrinal sobre el abandono divino. Jehová es mi pastor; nada me faltará en el Salmo 23 es una metáfora; David no es literalmente una oveja. Lea los Salmos como proposiciones doctrinales planas y predicará abstracciones donde el salmista quiso arrancar lágrimas. Léalos como poesía — con la imagen, el sentimiento, y la forma intactos — y enseñarán a su pueblo a orar.

blocks.en: Wisdom literature has its own rules too. Proverbs are observations of how the world usually works under God’s rule. They are not absolute promises. Train up a child in the way he should go, and when he is old he will not depart from it describes a general pattern. It is not a guarantee that obedient parents will never raise prodigals. The genre of Proverbs requires the pastor to teach the proverb and also to make room for the exception — or his people will be crushed when life proves the proverb’s limits. Ecclesiastes warns this is so: The race is not to the swift, nor the battle to the strong; time and chance happen to them all.
blocks.es_reference: La literatura sapiencial también tiene sus propias reglas. Los Proverbios son observaciones de cómo funciona usualmente el mundo bajo el gobierno de Dios. No son promesas absolutas. Instruye al niño en su carrera, aun cuando fuere viejo no se apartará de ella describe un patrón general. No es una garantía de que los padres obedientes nunca criarán pródigos. El género de los Proverbios requiere que el pastor enseñe el proverbio y también deje espacio para la excepción — o su pueblo será aplastado cuando la vida pruebe los límites del proverbio. Eclesiastés advierte que así es: la carrera no es de los ligeros, ni la guerra de los valientes; tiempo y ocasión acontecen a todos.

blocks.en: 8. Three Rules of Thumb
blocks.es_reference: 8. Tres reglas prácticas

blocks.en: Read a passage in its book. A verse pulled out of Hosea will not behave like a verse pulled out of Romans, even if both are in your concordance under the same word. Hosea is prophecy. Romans is epistle. Their rules differ. The book is the first signal of the genre.
blocks.es_reference: Lea un pasaje en su libro. Un versículo sacado de Oseas no se comportará como un versículo sacado de Romanos, aun si ambos están en su concordancia bajo la misma palabra. Oseas es profecía. Romanos es epístola. Sus reglas son distintas. El libro es la primera señal del género.

blocks.en: Identify the genre before you ask the meaning. Stop, name the kind of literature, then read. Is this a song? A parable? A chronicle? A personal letter? A prophetic oracle? An apocalyptic vision? The answer will set the rules. Most interpretive errors trace back to a pastor who skipped this step.
blocks.es_reference: Identifique el género antes de preguntar el significado. Deténgase, nombre la clase de literatura, luego lea. ¿Es esto una canción? ¿Una parábola? ¿Una crónica? ¿Una carta personal? ¿Un oráculo profético? ¿Una visión apocalíptica? La respuesta fijará las reglas. La mayoría de los errores interpretativos se remontan a un pastor que se saltó este paso.

blocks.en: Let the genre’s rules govern your sermon. A narrative sermon shows. A poetic sermon evokes. A wisdom sermon observes patterns and respects exceptions. A prophetic sermon confronts. An epistolary sermon argues from doctrine to application. A pastor whose every sermon sounds the same probably is not honoring genre. The Bible itself does not sound the same from book to book. It sounds like the genre God chose for that book.
blocks.es_reference: Deje que las reglas del género gobiernen su sermón. Un sermón narrativo muestra. Un sermón poético evoca. Un sermón de sabiduría observa patrones y respeta excepciones. Un sermón profético confronta. Un sermón epistolar argumenta de la doctrina a la aplicación. Un pastor cuyos sermones suenan todos iguales probablemente no está honrando el género. La Biblia misma no suena igual de libro a libro. Suena como el género que Dios escogió para ese libro.

blocks.en: 9. What Genre Awareness Saves You From
blocks.es_reference: 9. De qué le salva la conciencia del género

blocks.en: Three errors plague the pastor who flattens every text into the same shape. Treating poetry as propositional doctrine. The Psalmist cries; the pastor systematizes; the congregation goes home with a footnote instead of a song. Treating narrative as moral fable. The story of Ruth is reduced to be loyal like Ruth; the story of David and Goliath is reduced to face your giants; the gospel falls out of the story while the moralism stays. Treating prophecy as private prediction. Apocalyptic visions become end-times timelines; symbolic actions become merely strange anecdotes; the covenant warnings they actually carried get lost under speculation.
blocks.es_reference: Tres errores plagan al pastor que aplana cada texto a la misma forma. Tratar la poesía como doctrina proposicional. El salmista clama; el pastor sistematiza; la congregación se va a casa con una nota al pie en lugar de una canción. Tratar la narrativa como fábula moral. La historia de Rut se reduce a sea leal como Rut; la historia de David y Goliat se reduce a enfrente sus gigantes; el evangelio se cae de la historia mientras el moralismo se queda. Tratar la profecía como predicción privada. Las visiones apocalípticas se vuelven cronogramas del fin de los tiempos; las acciones simbólicas se vuelven meras anécdotas extrañas; las advertencias del pacto que en realidad cargaban se pierden bajo la especulación.

blocks.en: Each of these failures starts with the same omission. The pastor skipped the genre question. He hurried to ask what does it mean? before he asked what kind of thing is it? Slow down. Read the book first. Name the genre. Then ask the meaning. The text will yield more, not less.
blocks.es_reference: Cada una de estas fallas comienza con la misma omisión. El pastor se saltó la pregunta del género. Se apresuró a preguntar ¿qué significa? antes de preguntar ¿qué clase de cosa es? Disminuya la velocidad. Lea primero el libro. Nombre el género. Luego pregunte el significado. El texto cederá más, no menos.

blocks.en: 10. Read the Library Like a Library
blocks.es_reference: 10. Lea la biblioteca como una biblioteca

blocks.en: A pastor who walks into a public library and tries to read a poetry collection the way he reads a phone directory will fail at both. A pastor who walks into the Bible and tries to read Hosea the way he reads Romans, or Ruth the way he reads Psalms, will fail in the same way. The Bible is a library. The God who breathed it out chose many genres on purpose. Each is a different way of getting the truth into the human heart. Each requires the reader to slow down at the threshold of the book and ask, what kind of room am I walking into?
blocks.es_reference: Un pastor que entra a una biblioteca pública y trata de leer una colección de poesía de la manera en que lee un directorio telefónico fracasará en ambos. Un pastor que entra a la Biblia y trata de leer Oseas de la manera en que lee Romanos, o Rut de la manera en que lee los Salmos, fracasará de la misma manera. La Biblia es una biblioteca. El Dios que la exhaló escogió muchos géneros a propósito. Cada uno es una manera distinta de meter la verdad en el corazón humano. Cada uno requiere que el lector disminuya la velocidad en el umbral del libro y pregunte: ¿a qué clase de cuarto estoy entrando?

blocks.en: Pastor, your people need a pastor who reads the library like a library. They need Hosea preached as prophecy, Ruth preached as narrative, the Psalms preached as poetry, Proverbs preached as wisdom, Romans preached as the urgent pastoral letter that it is. The God who chose those genres will reward your respect for them by speaking through each one in its own voice. The same gospel of unforgivable forgiveness that Hosea preached in a marriage, Ruth preached in a love story, and Jesus preached in a parable, will preach through your sermons too — if you let each genre say it in its own way.
blocks.es_reference: Pastor, su pueblo necesita un pastor que lea la biblioteca como una biblioteca. Necesitan a Oseas predicado como profecía, a Rut predicada como narrativa, a los Salmos predicados como poesía, a los Proverbios predicados como sabiduría, a Romanos predicado como la carta pastoral urgente que es. El Dios que escogió esos géneros recompensará su respeto por ellos hablando a través de cada uno con su propia voz. El mismo evangelio del perdón imperdonable que Oseas predicó en un matrimonio, Rut predicó en una historia de amor, y Jesús predicó en una parábola, predicará también a través de sus sermones — si deja que cada género lo diga a su propia manera.

mc.stem: According to this unit, the question a pastor must ask BEFORE asking what a passage means is:
options: Which translation am I reading?
How long is the passage?
What kind of writing am I reading?
Has this passage been preached before?
mc.why: Correct. The genre question is the question before the question. A poem is not read like an epistle. A parable is not read like a chronicle. Identify the kind of literature first, and the passage opens to you in its own way.

mc.stem: The central principle of this unit is:
options: Every Bible passage should be preached the same way
Genre determines interpretation
Modern translations should be avoided
Only the New Testament has clear genres
mc.why: Correct. Identify the kind of literature before you ask what it means, and the passage will open to you in its own way. Force every passage into the same template and you will distort more than you preach.

mc.stem: The lesson names six main biblical genres. Which list correctly names them?
options: Hebrew, Greek, Aramaic, Latin, English, Spanish
Old, New, Apocrypha, Tradition, Liturgy, Creed
Devotional, Practical, Theological, Historical, Inspirational, Doctrinal
Narrative, Law, Wisdom, Poetry, Prophecy, Epistles
mc.why: Correct. Each of the six has its own reading rules. The pastor who treats a Proverb as if it were a Romans-style absolute promise will be wounded by life. The pastor who treats Revelation as a newspaper headline will embarrass the Lord. Genre is the corrective.

mc.stem: When God commands Hosea to marry Gomer (Hosea 1:2), the lesson teaches we should read this as:
options: A prophetic symbolic action — the prophet's marriage is the sermon
A heartbreaking private domestic anecdote
An ethical dilemma we must defend God against
A coincidence that has nothing to do with Israel
mc.why: Correct. Biblical prophecy regularly uses symbolic actions — Isaiah walked barefoot for three years, Jeremiah wore a yoke, Ezekiel lay on his side. Hosea's entire marriage is a prophetic sign. The marriage IS the sermon.

mc.stem: The names of Hosea's three children (Jezreel, Lo-Ruhamah, Lo-Ammi) function in the book as:
options: Random personal names of the family
Three ordinary Hebrew names with no significance
Names chosen for grandparents
Prophetic announcements of judgment: God will scatter, no longer pitied, not My people
mc.why: Correct. The children's names announce judgment on Israel. In the prophetic genre, the prophet's family becomes the sermon-board — names, marriage, and household actions all preach the covenant message God is delivering.

mc.stem: Hosea pays fifteen pieces of silver and barley to buy Gomer back from the slave market (Hosea 3:2). The lesson says this price was:
options: Double the normal slave price
Half the normal slave price — sin had taken its toll on what she fetched at auction
The exact price required by Mosaic law
A symbolic number with no real economic meaning
mc.why: Correct. Exodus 21:32 records the standard price of a slave as thirty shekels of silver. Hosea paid roughly half — sin had visibly devalued his wife in the slave market. He still bought her back. That is what God does for Israel and for us.

mc.stem: According to the lesson, the gospel of Hosea is summarized in the line:
options: "Hosea is a more patient husband than most men"
"Marriage is the most important institution in Israel"
"God is the One who buys back what shame has unmade"
"All prophets had difficult marriages"
mc.why: Correct. Once you read Hosea as prophecy, the marriage stops being a private story and starts being the gospel made visible. God is the One who buys back what shame has unmade. That is the truth Hosea's marriage was sent to preach.

mc.stem: The book of Ruth is identified in this lesson as an example of:
options: Prophetic apocalypse
Wisdom literature
Theological narrative — story carrying redemption through structure and names
A Mosaic legal code
mc.why: Correct. Ruth is narrative — story told as theology. Names carry meaning. Structure carries weight. The book begins with three deaths in Moab and ends with a birth in Bethlehem in the line of David. No proof-text in the middle; the whole shape of the four chapters preaches.

mc.stem: In Ruth, Naomi asks to be renamed "Mara." The lesson explains this as:
options: A narrator's device — Naomi means "pleasure"; Mara means "bitter"; the change preaches theology through a name
A nickname her grandchildren gave her
An ancient Hebrew custom required at every funeral
A mistranslation of the original text
mc.why: Correct. "Do not call me Pleasure; call me Bitter, because the Almighty has dealt bitterly with me." In narrative genre, names carry theology. Naomi's renaming is the narrator preaching her grief through her name itself.

mc.stem: The lesson identifies the structural arc of Ruth as:
options: Three deaths in Moab become one birth in Bethlehem in the line of the Messiah
A romance that begins and ends happily without theological weight
A legal proceeding from start to finish
A chronological war chronicle
mc.why: Correct. The narrative moves from three deaths in Moab to one birth in Bethlehem. The famine of chapter one is gone by chapter four. The bitterness of the opening becomes the blessing of the close — and the grandson is in the line of David and of Christ.

mc.stem: The lesson warns that the greatest temptation when preaching Ruth is to:
options: Read it in Hebrew
Flatten it into a moral fable — "be loyal like Ruth" — and lose the redemption story
Skip it entirely
Translate every name into English
mc.why: Correct. The narrative genre is not a moral fable. Ruth is not asking you to admire her loyalty; it is showing you the Redeemer who is coming to do for His people what Boaz did for Ruth — notice the foreigner, cover her, pay the price, bring her into the family.

mc.stem: The lesson compares the Prodigal Son (Luke 15) with Hosea (Hosea 1-3) to teach:
options: The same gospel of unforgivable forgiveness is preached in two different genres — parable and prophetic enacted biography
The Prodigal Son is the better story
Hosea is a Christian rewrite of the Prodigal
The two stories contradict each other
mc.why: Correct. The same gospel sounds different in different genres. The Prodigal Son comes to himself and repents; Gomer is simply bought back and loved again. Repentance and pursuit — two truths necessary to the gospel, each preached in the genre best suited to deliver it.

mc.stem: The most important difference between the Prodigal Son's return and Gomer's return, according to the lesson, is:
options: The Prodigal returns home; Gomer never returns home
The Prodigal Son was Jewish; Gomer was not
The Prodigal Son came to himself and repented; the text says Gomer's husband simply bought her back and loved her again
They lived in different historical periods
mc.why: Correct. In one genre, redemption is preached through the sinner's return; in another, redemption is preached through the husband's pursuit. Both are true, and the Bible needs both, and each genre tells the truth its form was built to tell.

mc.stem: According to this lesson, when reading the Psalms the pastor must remember:
options: The Psalms are scientific manuals
The Psalms are flat doctrinal propositions
The Psalms are poetry — image, parallel lines, emotion
The Psalms are legal codes
mc.why: Correct. Read "Why have You forsaken me?" as a poet's cry, not as doctrine about divine abandonment. Read "The Lord is my shepherd" as metaphor, not as zoology. Read the Psalms as poetry and they will teach your people to pray.

mc.stem: The lesson warns that reading Proverbs 22:6 ("Train up a child in the way he should go...") as an ABSOLUTE PROMISE will:
options: Wound the obedient parent whose child still becomes a prodigal
Always succeed without exception
Improve every child's behavior
Replace the need for parenting
mc.why: Correct. Proverbs are observations of how the world USUALLY works under God's rule, not absolute guarantees. Reading them as guarantees crushes parents whose obedient diligence still produces a wayward child. The genre requires room for the exception.

mc.stem: The lesson's first rule of thumb for honoring genre is:
options: Memorize verses in Greek
Read a passage in its book
Avoid commentaries
Translate the verse into multiple languages
mc.why: Correct. A verse pulled out of Hosea will not behave like a verse pulled out of Romans. The book is the first signal of the genre. Read the passage in its book and you have already done most of the genre work.

mc.stem: The lesson identifies three errors a pastor who flattens every text into the same shape will fall into. Which is NOT one of those three?
options: Treating poetry as propositional doctrine
Treating narrative as moral fable
Treating prophecy as private prediction
Treating the Bible as a library of many genres
mc.why: Correct. Treating the Bible as a library of many genres is exactly what the lesson RECOMMENDS — that is the solution, not the problem. The three ERRORS are flattening poetry into doctrine, narrative into moralism, and prophecy into prediction.

mc.stem: The lesson teaches that a pastor whose every sermon SOUNDS THE SAME is probably:
options: A very disciplined preacher
Not honoring genre — the Bible itself does not sound the same from book to book
Preaching too long
Using too many illustrations
mc.why: Correct. A narrative sermon shows. A poetic sermon evokes. A wisdom sermon observes patterns and respects exceptions. A prophetic sermon confronts. An epistolary sermon argues from doctrine to application. Sameness across all sermons is the symptom of flattened genre.

mc.stem: The closing image of this unit compares the Bible to:
options: A single book with one unified literary style
A textbook on theology
A historical archive of one type of document
A library — many genres each read in its own way
mc.why: Correct. The Bible is a library. The God who breathed it out chose many genres on purpose. The pastor who walks into the Bible and tries to read Hosea like Romans, or Ruth like Psalms, fails at both. Each room of the library asks to be read its own way.

mc.stem: The closing charge of this unit to the pastor is:
options: Pick one favorite genre and preach only from it
Avoid all prophecy and apocalypse
Treat every text the same way for consistency
Read the library like a library — let each genre say the gospel in its own way
mc.why: Correct. The same gospel of unforgivable forgiveness that Hosea preached in a marriage, Ruth preached in a love story, and Jesus preached in a parable, will preach through your sermons too — IF you let each genre say it in its own way.

fill.prompt: The principle of this unit is that ____ determines interpretation: identify the kind of literature before you ask what it means.
The Bible is not one genre; it is a ____ of many genres bound between two covers.
God commanded the prophet Hosea to marry ____, a prostitute, and later to buy her back from the slave market.
Hosea's third child was named ____, meaning "not My people."
Hosea is not autobiography but prophecy: like Isaiah walking barefoot or Jeremiah wearing a wooden yoke, his entire marriage is a prophetic ____, and the marriage is the sermon.
Ruth and Boaz had a son named Obed, who became the grandfather of King ____.
Naomi, whose name means ____, asked on her return to Bethlehem to be renamed Mara, meaning bitter.
In Hebrew poetry, lines come in ____ pairs: the second line restates, intensifies, or contrasts the first.
Proverbs are observations of how the world usually works under God's rule; they are not absolute ____.
Reducing the story of Ruth to "be loyal like Ruth" is the error of treating narrative as a moral ____, like one of Aesop's.

sa.prompt: State in your own words the central principle of this unit, and explain why "what kind of writing am I reading?" must come before "what does this mean?"
sa.model: The central principle is that genre determines interpretation: the kind of writing decides the rules for reading it. 'What kind of writing am I reading?' must come before 'What does this mean?' because the same words mean different things in a law, a poem, a proverb, or a narrative. Identify the genre first, then the meaning.

sa.prompt: List the six main biblical genres named in this lesson, and briefly describe what makes each one distinct.
sa.model: The lesson names six main biblical genres: narrative, which tells what happened; law, which commands; wisdom, which observes how life works; poetry, which sings in parallel lines and images; prophecy, which announces God's word in symbol and oracle; and epistles, which argue and instruct. Each genre is distinct and read by its own rules.

sa.prompt: Explain why Hosea must be read as PROPHECY rather than as autobiography, and what the prophetic genre unlocks in the book that autobiography would miss.
sa.model: Hosea must be read as prophecy, not autobiography. His marriage to Gomer is a symbolic action — an enacted sermon to Israel — not merely one ancient pastor's hard marriage. Read as autobiography it becomes a debate about whether God told a man to marry a prostitute. Read in its prophetic genre, every painful detail becomes theology about God and unfaithful Israel.

sa.prompt: Trace what Hosea's marriage to Gomer preaches theologically: name Gomer's role, Hosea's role, the meaning of the children's names, and what the redemption from the slave market signifies.
sa.model: Hosea's marriage preaches theology. Gomer plays the part of Israel, the unfaithful wife; Hosea plays the part of God, the faithful husband. The children's names announce judgment on Israel. And when Hosea buys Gomer back from the slave market, it signifies God redeeming His people out of bondage — buying back the unfaithful at a price.

sa.prompt: Explain why Ruth is identified as theological narrative, and describe how the names (Elimelech, Naomi, Mahlon, Chilion, Ruth, Mara) carry the theology of the book.
sa.model: Ruth is theological narrative — a story that preaches without symbolic visions. Even the names carry the theology: Naomi means 'pleasant,' but when she returns empty from Moab she calls herself Mara, meaning 'bitter.' The movement from pleasant to bitter and back to blessing is the theology of redemption told in narrative form.

sa.prompt: Describe the structural arc of Ruth (from Moab to Bethlehem) and explain how the structure itself is the theology in narrative genre.
sa.model: Ruth's structure is its theology. The book begins with a famine and three deaths in Moab and ends with a birth in Bethlehem — the famine becomes fullness, the bitterness becomes blessing. The child born is Obed, grandfather of David, in the line of the Messiah. The very shape of the narrative, from emptiness to fullness, preaches redemption.

sa.prompt: Compare the Prodigal Son (Luke 15) with Hosea (Hosea 1-3) to show how the same gospel is preached through two different genres. Identify the key theological difference between the two stories.
sa.model: The Prodigal Son (a parable) and Hosea (prophecy) preach the same gospel of a faithful love that takes back the unfaithful, but through two different genres. The key theological difference is the cost shown: the Prodigal's father runs in welcoming grace, while Hosea must buy Gomer back from the slave market — the same redeeming love, one told as parable, one as enacted prophecy.

sa.prompt: Explain the danger of reading Hebrew poetry (the Psalms) as flat doctrinal propositions, and describe what the poetic genre requires the pastor to honor.
sa.model: Reading Hebrew poetry — the Psalms — as flat doctrinal propositions misses how it works. Poetry speaks in parallel lines that restate and intensify, in compressed images and metaphor, and it gives emotion room to speak. The poetic genre requires the pastor to honor the parallelism, the imagery, and the feeling, not to flatten a psalm into a list of propositions.

sa.prompt: Explain why Proverbs should NOT be read as absolute promises, using Proverbs 22:6 ("Train up a child...") as an example. What pastoral damage results when the genre is misread?
sa.model: Proverbs are observations of how life usually works under God's rule, not absolute promises. 'Train up a child in the way he should go' (22:6) is a general pattern, not a guarantee, and there are exceptions. Read as an iron promise it does pastoral damage — wounding a faithful parent whose grown child has strayed by telling them they must have failed.

sa.prompt: State and explain the lesson's closing image: "Read the library like a library." What does this charge require the pastor to do every week in sermon preparation?
sa.model: The closing image is 'read the library like a library.' The Bible is a library of many genres God chose on purpose, each a different way of getting truth into the heart. As a reader would not read poetry like a phone directory, the pastor must pause at the threshold of each book and read each genre its own way before he preaches it.
